title: What is a code review?
summary: Why teams review each other's code and what a reviewer is looking for.
objectives: Explain what a code review is and why teams do it
Name the main things a reviewer checks
Know the three steps of a review: read, comment, decide

sections.heading: Reviewing is reading with a purpose
sections.text: Before code is merged into the main project, a teammate reads it in a pull request. The goal is not to find someone to blame, but to catch problems early and share knowledge. A bug found in review costs minutes; the same bug found by users can cost days.

sections.heading: What a reviewer checks
points: Correctness: does the code do what the requirements say?
Edge cases: what happens with empty, very large or unexpected input?
Readability: can a teammate understand it without asking?
Tests: do the tests prove that it works?

sections.heading: The three steps
sections.text: Every review in Code Croak follows the same steps as a real pull request: read the code next to the requirements, leave comments on specific lines, and make a decision: approve or request changes.

takeaway: A review is about the code, not the person. You are helping your teammate ship something better.

title: Reading code against requirements
summary: How to check if a function really does what it promises.
objectives: Compare code line by line with its requirements
Trace an example input through a function
Spot off-by-one errors and missing edge cases

sections.heading: Start with the requirements
sections.text: Read the requirements before the code. For each requirement, find the line that handles it. If you cannot find one, that is already a review comment.

sections.heading: Run the example in your head
sections.text: Take the example input and follow it through the code, step by step. Write down the value of each variable. Off-by-one errors usually show up here: a loop that starts at 1 instead of 0 skips the first item.

sections.heading: Think about the edges
points: What if the list is empty?
What if there is only one item?
What if a value is 0 or negative?

takeaway: "It runs without errors" is not the same as "it is correct". Always check the result.

title: Clean, readable code
summary: Code that works can still be hard to read or change.
objectives: Suggest a concrete improvement instead of only criticising

sections.heading: Names should explain meaning
sections.text: Short names like s, g or check force readers to work out what they mean. A good name tells you what a value is or what a function does, so the code reads almost like a sentence.

sections.heading: Avoid magic numbers
sections.text: A number like 20 hidden in a calculation does not say what it is. Put it in a named constant such as TOTAL_LESSONS, so the next person knows what to change.

takeaway: When code works, review it for the next person who has to read or change it.

title: Reviewing tests
summary: A green test run does not always mean the tests are good.
objectives: Check if a test expects the right result
Find requirements that have no test

sections.heading: Read the name, then the expectation
sections.text: A test name says what should happen. Check that the expectation really matches it. A test called "rejects a short password" that expects true will pass when the code is broken.

sections.heading: Every requirement needs a test
points: Find a test for each one
Missing test? Suggest one with a concrete example

takeaway: Tests are code too. Review them as carefully as the feature itself.

title: Writing helpful review comments
summary: How to give feedback that is clear, kind and easy to act on.
objectives: Point to a specific line and explain the impact
Suggest a fix or ask a question
Choose between approve and request changes

sections.heading: A good comment has three parts
points: Why: what goes wrong, with an example
What next: a suggestion or a question

sections.heading: Keep the tone friendly
sections.text: Start with what is good, talk about the code instead of the person, and phrase fixes as questions: "Could we start the loop at 0?" works better than "This is wrong."

sections.heading: Make the decision
sections.text: Approve when the code meets all requirements. Request changes when something must be fixed before merging. Small style tips alone are usually not a reason to block.

takeaway: The best review comments teach something, not only point out a mistake.
